findings.title: Configuration freeze can permanently bless Multicall3 or any arbitrary adapter
findings.requirement: Multicall3 must be impossible to register or approve, and an arbitrary malicious adapter must be impossible to execute after configuration is frozen.
findings.evidence: registerAdapter accepts every nonzero address. freezeConfiguration records no adapter identity/code hash and does not require registered adapters to be frozen. The named Multicall3 test only exercises the default unregistered state.
findings.reproduction: As owner, call registerAdapter(0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11), then freezeConfiguration(); allowedAdapters(MULTICALL3) remains true. The same sequence works for any contract implementing IAdapter.
findings.consequence: The stated frozen security boundary does not establish that only the reviewed adapters are reachable. SweepExecutor can transiently approve a forbidden or malicious registered address and call it during a sweep.
findings.remediation: Reject Multicall3 explicitly and freeze only a verified adapter set whose identities/code hashes and frozen states are validated, or replace arbitrary owner registration with immutable typed adapter slots.
findings.regression_test_required: Prove Multicall3 registration reverts regardless of address case; prove unknown adapter registration/freeze is impossible; prove every reachable adapter is itself frozen before executor freeze.

findings.title: Freeze permits empty, invalid, or independently mutable configurations
findings.requirement: Zero/invalid configurations must not accidentally freeze and adapter routing configuration must not remain mutable after executor freeze.
findings.evidence: freezeConfiguration unconditionally sets a boolean. Both adapters likewise freeze without readiness checks, while SweepExecutor does not verify their configurationFrozen values.
findings.reproduction: Immediately after deployment call freezeConfiguration; it succeeds with no registered swap adapter and only the constructor's native-output sentinel. Register a mutable adapter before freeze and observe its own intermediate-token registry can still change afterward.
findings.consequence: A deployment may be permanently unusable or may claim a frozen boundary while a reachable adapter remains owner-mutable.
findings.remediation: Define and enforce readiness invariants and require all registered adapters to be frozen before freezing SweepExecutor.
findings.regression_test_required: Freeze-empty/invalid reverts; executor freeze with mutable adapter reverts; valid fully frozen configuration succeeds.

findings.title: Multicall3 can be selected as plan recipient despite a completed prohibition claim
findings.requirement: Multicall3 must not be used as recipient.
findings.evidence: Only the zero recipient is rejected. ERC-20 output is transferred to plan.recipient at line 341 and native output is called at line 335. docs/requirements-traceability.md marks the broader prohibition implemented.
findings.reproduction: Build a valid signed plan with recipient 0xcA11bde05977b3631167028862bE2a173976CA11; no recipient-specific guard rejects it.
findings.consequence: The implemented contract and completed traceability claim disagree; funds may be sent to an infrastructure address the security model says must never receive them.
findings.remediation: Either enforce the forbidden recipient in the contract/shared validation or narrow and correct the requirement with explicit rationale.
findings.regression_test_required: ERC-20 and native-output plans with Multicall3 recipient must follow the resolved policy.

findings.title: Required execution-plan field sensitivity is not retained in repository tests
findings.requirement: Mutating chain, executor, owner, recipient, output token, amount, adapter, route bytes, minimum output, deadline, nonce, and action order must change the hash.
findings.evidence: Solidity tests omit owner, adapter, routeData, and minAmountOut mutations; TypeScript tests omit owner, adapter, routeData, and minAmountOut. An independent temporary Node mutation run confirmed the current implementation changes for all required fields, but this protection is not retained as regression coverage.
findings.reproduction: Inspect test names in SweepPlanLib.t.sol and executionPlanHash.test.ts; only the subset reported above is present.
findings.consequence: Future cross-language or field-omission regressions can pass the committed golden-vector suites.
findings.remediation: Add one-field mutation tests on both Solidity and TypeScript sides for every required field.

findings.title: PriceService/oracle deferral lacks a tracked phase acceptance test
findings.requirement: Deferred pricing/oracle requirements must be explicitly assigned to a later phase and acceptance test.
findings.evidence: pricing-and-oracle-model.md describes the design, but implementation-plan.md and requirements-traceability.md do not name PriceService, oracle freshness/confidence, executable-route versus reference value, or acceptance tests.
findings.reproduction: Search implementation-plan.md and requirements-traceability.md for PriceService, Pyth, MON/USD, freshness, or confidence; the required tracked gate is absent.
findings.consequence: A later phase can satisfy the formal gate without implementing or testing the promised pricing boundary.
findings.remediation: Add explicit phase ownership and acceptance tests for route valuation, oracle reference values, stale/low-confidence rejection, and minAmountOut independence.
findings.regression_test_required: Tracked acceptance cases listed in remediation.

findings.title: Generic-token deferral is incompletely tracked
findings.requirement: Future production support must include manual arbitrary-token assessment and must not use demo addresses as a support allowlist.
findings.evidence: token-support-model.md states these requirements, but the formal plan/traceability gates track discovery and assessment without manual-entry and negative demo-allowlist acceptance tests.
findings.reproduction: Search the plan and traceability matrix for manual token address entry and a demo-only allowlist prohibition; no formal acceptance gate exists.
findings.consequence: A Phase 11/12 implementation could meet recorded gates while excluding arbitrary ERC-20s or silently using the demo set.
findings.remediation: Track both requirements and their negative/positive acceptance tests in the implementation plan and traceability matrix.
findings.regression_test_required: Manual arbitrary ERC-20 reaches assessment; demo addresses are not a production support filter.

findings.title: Repository-wide Multicall grep evidence is false
findings.requirement: Audit evidence and grep claims must be independently reproducible.
findings.evidence: The artifact reports no Multicall matches under packages/apps, but packages/contracts/test/SweepExecutor.t.sol contains the named Multicall3 test and verified address at lines 417 and 461-489. The same absolute claim appears in security-addendum-review.md and findings.md.
findings.consequence: The evidence package cannot substantiate its absolute absence claim and overstates review reliability.
findings.remediation: Record actual output and distinguish production, test, documentation, generated, and vendored matches.
findings.regression_test_required: Evidence-generation check that preserves and classifies all matches.

findings.title: Reported Solidity formatting verification does not reproduce
findings.requirement: Claimed formatting and verification commands must pass independently.
findings.evidence: Running forge fmt --check from packages/contracts exits 1 and prints diffs in production contracts and tests. The artifact reports PASS.
findings.consequence: The addendum verification report is inaccurate and the required command is failing.
findings.remediation: Apply forge formatting in a remediation pass and rerun the exact command from the contract root.
findings.regression_test_required: forge fmt --check in CI from packages/contracts.

findings.title: Traceability retains the obsolete execution hash and test total
findings.requirement: Traceability evidence must identify the current cross-language golden vector and suite count.
findings.evidence: The document cites 0x184bb27c... and 14 transaction-review tests; current evidence is 0xdf7a8dd0...5100d1 and 16 transaction-review tests.
findings.reproduction: Compare requirements-traceability.md with golden-vectors.md and pnpm test output.
findings.consequence: Reviewers are directed to stale Phase 2 evidence.
findings.remediation: Update the traceability row to current values while preserving historical notes separately.
findings.regression_test_required: Documentation consistency check against committed vector/test output.

findings.title: Security-addendum severity totals contradict their own table
findings.requirement: Reported finding totals must match row severities.
findings.evidence: F-17 is labeled P3 in the table but counted as P2 in the summary. Table labels total P2=3 and P3=2, while the summary reports P2=4 and P3=1.
findings.reproduction: Count the severity labels in findings.md and compare lines 35-37.
findings.consequence: The report's own severity accounting is unreliable.
findings.remediation: Correct either F-17 classification or the totals and explain the chosen severity.
findings.regression_test_required: Automated or reviewed table-summary consistency check.
